                                      PROJECT NO. 59142


 REVIEW OF ERCOT’s                                §               BEFORE THE
 INTERCONNECTION PROCESSES FOR                    §       PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION
 LARGE LOADS                                      §                OF TEXAS

     TRACT HOLDING COMPANY I, LLC’S COMMENTS ON THE COMMISSION’S STAFF
                        MEMO DATED APRIL 12, 2026

I.       Introduction

        Tract Holding Company I, LLC, on behalf of its affiliates, (“Tract”) appreciates the
opportunity to submit supplemental comments in response to the Public Utility Commission of
Texas (“Commission”) Staff Memorandum dated April 12, 2026 and filed in Project No. 59142
(“Staff Memo”).

II.      Study Validity

        The Staff Memo references ERCOT study validity on pages 2-3. This is a new concept not
included in the existing Planning Guide, which is the “law of the land” per Commission instruction.
Large loads that have completed existing Planning Guide or Nodal Protocol study processes should
not be subject to a new requirement that has not yet been approved by ERCOT’s Board or the
Commission. This is especially impactful for large load requests that have been in the study process
for a year or more, and that are awaiting results from ERCOT between now and July 24 – when
ERCOT has proposed that Transmission Service Providers (“TSPs”) must demonstrate complete
and valid studies. The studies containing those large load requests may be deemed invalid by
ERCOT after July 24, at which time the large load request would have no recourse to be included
in Batch Zero Base. Requiring a new “validity check” by ERCOT for studies completed between
now and July, even though no such concept exists in currently effective rules, raises the additional
question of why ERCOT would approve such studies if they were “invalid.” The imposition of
such requirements out of the control of the large load that otherwise meets all legally effective and
applicable standards is not supportive of business development, especially where that requirement
is subject to the ERCOT’s discretion and does not allow for notice, comment, or participation by
the large load customer. Instead, as previously directed, ERCOT should give full force and effect
to existing law and honor the completed studies of those large load requests who dutifully followed
legally effective and applicable requirements.

III.     Minimum Capacity Allocation

        The Staff Memo proposes that ERCOT should establish a 100 MW transmission capacity
allocation minimum for projects in the Batch Zero Study. Tract agrees with the concept but does
not have a recommendation at this time.

                                                 1
 IV.     Intermediate Project Maturity

        The Staff Memo proposes that, to be considered Base Load for Batch Zero for large loads
that have not yet issued a notice to proceed for construction to the utility, the large load must attest
to a contract with a tenant. This requirement is not called for by Senate Bill 6, has been made more
difficult by ERCOT’s introduction of PGRR 145 and the Commission’s proposed rulemaking in
Project No. 58481, and should be replaced with objective project-specific characteristics
recommended by Tract in its comments filed April 13, 2026 in Project No. 58481 (local zoning,
site ownership, long lead time equipment ordered). Senate Bill 6 does not require the Commission
to adopt Standards including a requirement for large loads to demonstrate contracts with tenants
to receive interconnection capacity. Contracts with tenants are not necessarily good indicators of
project maturity, as they can be cancelled, reduced, or transferred to other sites. Must the tenant be
investment grade? Can the tenant be an affiliate? What if the tenant lease contains provisions
allowing its early termination? And how will such information be verified?

        In addition, despite every effort by the large load customer to obtain such a contract, the
introduction of ERCOT’s PGRR 145 and the Commission’s proposed rules in Project No. 58481
have introduced regulatory uncertainty into the marketplace. Tenants have expressed a desire for
certainty regarding where a large load request will land under these new rules before entering into
a contract, precluding the ability of some large load requests, that have otherwise met all existing
requirements, from entering into contracts with tenants.
         However, Tract recognizes the Commission’s desire to remove “phantom loads” from those
in Batch Zero Base. To achieve this objective, the Commission should instead guide ERCOT to
use more site-specific, objectively verifiable demonstrations of project maturity. These could
include the Staff Memo’s proposal for “Advanced Project Maturity” regarding large load
attestation that long lead time equipment is ordered for timely delivery. These could also include
concepts Tract proposed in its comments filed on April 13, 2026 in Project No. 58481, such as
deed ownership or long-term lease of the site and local approvals, where required. These are
objective, verifiable, and demonstrate serious investment in the site’s ability to energize on-time.
These are the characteristics investors look to when deciding whether to finance construction of a
large load. Without these demonstrations, a simple contract with a tenant is insufficient to
demonstrate project maturity.


V.      Conclusion

       Tract appreciates consideration of these important comments as the Proposal for
Publication is being finalized.




                                                   2
     Respectfully Submitted,




    Orijit Ghoshal
    Vice President, Government and
    Regulatory Affairs
    3200 Cherry Creek Drive
    Denver, CO 80209

    April 16, 2026

 VI.    Executive Summary – Tract – (PROJECT NO. 59142)

This submission urges the Public Utility Commission of Texas to implement new large-load
interconnection standards in a manner that is prospective, consistent with Senate Bill 6, and
supportive of continued investment and reliability in Texas.

Opposition to Retroactive “Study Validity” Requirement
  • The Staff Memorandum introduces a new “study validity” concept not contained in the
      current ERCOT Planning Guide or Nodal Protocols.
  • Large load projects that have completed required studies under existing rules should not
      be subject to new, unapproved requirements.
  • Retroactive application risks invalidating studies completed after months or years of
      compliance, potentially excluding projects from Batch Zero Base with no recourse.
  • ERCOT should give full force and effect to completed studies conducted under currently
      effective law.

Concern Over Regulatory Uncertainty
   • Imposing discretionary, unapproved requirements controlled by ERCOT undermines
      predictability and business development.
   • Large load customers lack notice, comment rights, or participation in any new “validity”
      determinations.

Support for Minimum Capacity Allocation Concept
   • Tract supports the idea of establishing a minimum transmission capacity allocation (e.g.,
      100 MW) for Batch 0 projects but has no specific recommendation on the appropriate
      minimum level at this time.

Objection to Tenant Contract Requirement for Project Maturity
  • Requiring a tenant contract for large loads without a notice to proceed is not mandated by
      Senate Bill 6. Tenant contracts are an unreliable indicator of project maturity and raise
      unresolved questions (creditworthiness, affiliates, termination rights, verification).
  • Recent ERCOT and Commission actions (PGRR 145 and Project No. 58481) have
      increased regulatory uncertainty, limiting tenants’ willingness to contract.

Recommendation for Objective, Verifiable Maturity Criteria
   • The Commission should focus on site-specific, objectively verifiable indicators to
     eliminate “phantom loads.”
   • Appropriate indicators include:
         o Ownership or long-term control of the project site.
         o Local zoning and permitting approvals, where required.
         o Procurement of long lead-time equipment for timely delivery.
   • These criteria better demonstrate serious investment, on-time energization capability, and
     investor confidence than tenant contracts alone.
